note: Christmas Island is served by Westpac's branch there, and Westpac's Australian cards (Christmas Island is Australian territory, under Australia's credit law and its dollar). Westpac's own pages for every personal credit card it sells (read 30 October 2026) were read; other banks weren't read. The Low Rate card costs $7 a month and charges 13.74% a year on purchases; the Lite card $9 a month and 9.90%, with no cash advances, no foreign transaction fee and no missed-payment fee; the Low Fee card $30 a year, waived in its first year and in any year with $5,000 of purchases, and 20.99%. The Altitude Black and Platinum cards, each in a Rewards, Qantas and Velocity version, charge 23.98% a year on purchases, an annual card fee ($295 Black, $175 Platinum) and an annual rewards program fee ($75 Rewards; $155 Qantas and Velocity Black; $125 Qantas and Velocity Platinum). Every card but the Lite charges a cash advance rate (21.99% on Low Rate and Low Fee, 23.99% on Altitude), a 3.5% cash advance fee, a 3% foreign transaction fee and a $20 missed payment fee. Westpac's credit card changes page sets the minimum payment of the Lite, Low Rate and Low Fee cards at 2% of the closing balance or $10, whichever is greater, now, and lists changes from 30 November 2026: the Lite's fee rises to $10 a month and the Low Fee's to $45 a year (both written as changes); the purchase rates rise to 11.99%, 14.99% and 23.99%, the cash advance rate to 24.24%, and the minimum to 2.5% or $25, which the form can't schedule and aren't written; the Low Fee's spend waiver ends only for cards approved from that date, which the game can't tell apart, so it is kept. The Altitude cards' minimum payment isn't stated on their pages. The first-year fee waivers for existing Westpac customers and the balance transfer offers are introductory and not written.
